title: Bayer voluntarily withdraws Baycol
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, FDA Talk Paper T01-34, 8 August 2001
result: Bayer withdrew cerivastatin (Baycol), approved in the US in 1997, because of reports of sometimes fatal rhabdomyolysis, with FDA agreement. All statins had been associated with very rare reports of rhabdomyolysis, but fatal rhabdomyolysis was reported significantly more often with cerivastatin, most frequently at higher doses, in elderly patients and with gemfibrozil. FDA had received reports of 31 US deaths from severe rhabdomyolysis with cerivastatin, 12 with concomitant gemfibrozil. In rare cases muscle injury led to renal and other organ failure, which can be fatal; some patients reported no symptoms of muscle injury.
